items.note: S1.1 states that a fixed network of copy, gather, scatter and side-injection gates, run forward, inverse, forward, exchanges the banks up to sign and restores every scratch wire. It omits the forward invocation's effect y_S <- y_S + x_S, the explicit map (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a), the triples of [100] indexing the data, and the wire counts. There is no derivation: the cancellation (JV+RG)x and the central coefficients are not shown.

The plan states that a frame commutes with the pointwise gate, so only endpoint frames matter. It writes the result as D_out D_in^{-1}, dropping the scalar network S_Omega and the route sign eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1} (814-822). The per-edge operator D_v D_u^{-1} is left implicit.

Present and as in the paper: <t_S,t_T>=|S cap T|-1, the telescoping budget Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich and L_b/N=100/539. Missing: the terminal and gate label tables (883-889, eq:motif-labels) and the residual table, so 'only centre 3->4 decreases' is only quoted, not derived. Also missing are the binary labels of the complex network, L_c/N=101/539 and the orthonormal-basis claim, and N, m and h are never defined.

The rank sum s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b<W_b m is derived on the paper's route: rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, plus the N rank-one 2P_{U_a} exceptions. S1.3.4 loosely puts P_U 'at vertices', whereas the paper puts -P_{U_a} on X_a sources and zero on other sources. The endpoint identity is used in S1.5.3 but never checked (P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I).

S2.1 states one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector, s<Wm kernels in all, and C^{tensor m} on every role after corrections. It does not define the phase frames C_U, give s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c, or extend to k columns. There is no derivation (weight additivity mod 4, the Z-corrections on supp(u_a)).

The bit-network chain is given: L_b/N=100/539<1/2, then deficit N-2L_b>0, then s_b/W_b<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50} from deficit >20*2^{-50} and log m<20. The exact values eta_b and eta_c are not given. The complex saving s_c<W_c m with sigma appears only as 's<Wm' (S2.1) and a<=m^sigma (S2.6.3). The inequality m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta) is not shown.

The plan relies on 'linear-time controlled updates', 'the elementary stream operation' and cyclic row splitting (S1.5.1). It does not state the lemmas' content: O(V) digit permutations and moves, split/merge, and y -> y+a(controls) mod q^b with offsets computable in b^{O(1)}.

Present and as in the paper: A=E_1 Pi E_2, the order of the triangular transforms, and one interchange per one of Pi between two controlled updates, giving exactly a interchanges plus O(V). Omitted: the arithmetic is over Z/q^b with a fixed odd prime q avoiding the denominators, and H precedes D. The elimination proof of lem:lower-lower and the choice of q are not given.

Follows the proof step by step: k=0 case, cyclic row split, shear frames done by recursive interchanges, endpoint identity giving H<-H+D, the three-update interchange, s calls on volume V/W, the recurrence, the geometric sum and the fixed-tape schedule. The hypothesis that the row field length is divisible by W^k is missing from S1.5; it appears only later, in S1.6.2.

Same steps as the paper: high digits as the row field, padding to R'=W^k ceil(R/W^k)<2R, base-m pieces at cost O(V) sum a_j m^{j tau}=O(Ve^tau), and radix-q padding of binary chunks, giving O(Vu^tau).

Stated: exactly s_c child calls on f=e/m axes with no extra calls from inverse wrappers, M in GL(m,F_2) as at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, and H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D. Missing: the conjugation P_M X_v P_M^{-1}=X_{Mv} that moves residual directions onto coordinate slots (eq:phase-edge-coordinate), which is why binary basis changes arise, and the identity (C^{-1})^{tensor f}=(-i)^f Z C Z.

The XOR at j_i=rho+iK, delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}} and the time bound match the lemma. Not given: the parity-flip result of the eight lines (eq:eight-packed-result, with auxiliary w restored), the guard interval 10<=g<=2^{K-1}-11 and its union bound, the argument that T_0 S_0^{-1} permutes B, the restored third chunk z, and the separate top position j_{f-1}.

As in the paper: role streams of volume V/W, F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves O(e), internal sum O(e^lambda), leaf bound, base-m pieces and the condition on lambda'. Missing: rows come from the first q_0 chunks, padded to a multiple of W^{k_0} (2306-2323); q_0 is used but never defined.

Correct: O(Vd^{lambda'}), exact evaluation with p+ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) fractional bits (O(p) since eps C_1<1), and a single truncation with error <sqrt2 2^{-p}. The arithmetic-depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E behind the guard width is not derived, nor is the uniform cost of the packed calls. K=floor(d^c) is not stated.

Character cancellation, decimation in frequency, bit-reversed storage, grouped rounds with y^E, prefix moves, chunk exchanges and per-round layer cost follow the paper. The error claim <sqrt2 l 2^{-p} is stated but not derived (J_E commutes with Q_p, so one truncation per round contracts). The exact counterparts L B F^- and F^+ B^{-1} L^{-1} are only implicit (S3.4).
Same steps as the paper: B_0=2^{4p}, signed packing with carries in {-1,0}, |h_j|<B_0/2, centred extraction with carries in {0,1}, and four products giving O(rp log(rp)).
Keeps the common LB order (justified in S3's motivation), checks normalization via F^-(f*g)=M(F^-f)(F^-g), gets error M(3 delta+eta)=sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^{-p}, and states the cost as in the paper.

Derived as in the paper: T P_s F_s=P_t F_t S, the Neumann series for N=CTD, A=S' and B_0=D'J'C, and the tensor form with gamma=2d alpha^2 and the costs. Missing: the hypothesis theta=t/s-1>p/alpha^4 (and why alpha^2 theta>1), the definitions of P_s and P_t, and the approximation errors <p^2 per line and <dp^2 in total.

Chirp periodicity, coefficient comparison with QF_t, R_c^{-1}F^+ = F^+ R_c by substitution, and the convolution rule giving (u*v)/S^2 follow the paper. Only the conjugation remark for RF^+ is omitted.

Fixed constants, sizes, Tp=Theta(n), alpha and gamma=o(b), and primes with T/2<S<T are given. Missing: delta=1/16 and eta=1/(4d). Neither the Bernoulli bound nor the check alpha^4 theta_i>p is derived; S5.7 only asserts that the hypotheses hold. The n^{o(1)} prime search appears only in the method.

Uses the map x -> prod x_i^{mu_i} with mu_i=P_i^{-1} mod s_i, shows it is an isomorphism, gives the triangular coordinates b_i, implements them as prefix-controlled cyclic shifts that keep padding zero, and gets O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)) with O(d^2) interchanges.

The exact isomorphism x_d -> zeta y and the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j are derived as in the paper. Missing: the normalized identity M_C(f,g)=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T and the computed twist with errors below 4*2^{-p}.

The source transform (A, chirp transform, B_0, scale by 2^gamma, exact counterpart RF_s) and the six operations follow the paper; S8.8 explains the two scales by S correctly. The method line of S8 misattributes them (see errors), and RF^+ by conjugation is not mentioned.

E_ring<5TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, E_w<28*2^gamma T^2 L, the final bound <448b 2^{-3b/4}<1/2, rounding and carries are all correct. The intermediate complex-convolution (6TL) and chirp (8TL) error steps are skipped, as is most of the disk-margin bookkeeping.

Normalization by V=Tp, min margin g_2=eps c(1-tau)=2^{-181}=2 kappa, log factors <=p^kappa, the final bound and the schoolbook cutoff are correct. Only three of the seven rows are given (dK, pK^{tau-1}, l d^{lambda'}); CRT and axis layouts, Gaussian line maps, chirps and packed products are not, nor are the o(V) setup and exceptional-sorting bounds.

S0 says the bound disproves the n log n optimality conjecture in this model. It does not state what the negation requires (one machine with liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0) or that the bound gives limit zero.

errors.says: Along a route only the endpoint operator D_out D_in^{-1} remains.
errors.paper: The implemented operator is D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}; a route w -> rho(w) applies eps_w D_sink(rho(w)) D_source(w)^{-1}, so the scalar routing and sign stay in the formula.

errors.says: Method: one scale by S undoes the transform normalization and the second undoes the digit scaling.
errors.paper: After the three transforms the exact result is (u*v)/S^2. The first S gives w=(u*v)/S. In the second scale 2^{2b+4}S, the factor S removes the remaining normalization and 2^{2b+4} undoes the two input digit scales.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). S1 builds the interchange from the bit network: exchange, frames, labels and rank budget s<Wm, shear lemma, the recurrence F_k=O(e^tau), and general widths. S2 builds the layer from the complex network, S3-S4 the synthetic transforms, ring convolution, resampling and chirp, and S5-S10 the parameters, algorithm, exact recovery and cost table with min margin 2^{-181}=2 kappa. It thins out at the network itself (h=100, N, m and the triple indexing are never defined, and the label tables behind 'only centre 3->4 decreases' are only quoted), at the complex network (S2.1 is a single quoted step with no phase frames, no s_c formula and no P_M conjugation), and in the cost table, which gives three of seven rows.

steps.note: S1.1 gives the gate types, the forward/inverse/forward stages, the exchange up to sign and scratch restoration. The defining parameters are absent throughout the plan: h=100, data pairs indexed by triples, N=C(h,3)^3 and m=h^3. The exact map (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a) is not written. Judged conservatively as mentioned.

S1.2 has the mechanism: one invertible frame per gate commutes with the pointwise gate, so only endpoint frames act, and S1's method makes each edge a change of frame (an address shear). The scalar network S is dropped from the formula (D_out D_in^{-1}), a minor looseness.

Labels are subspaces of an m-dimensional space built from tensor products of triple indicator vectors. Neighbouring triple lines are orthogonal and nondegenerate, adjacent labels are nested, and the only decreasing edges are the central wires from time 3 to 4, each losing h.
S1.3.4.1 gives rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U for nested labels. S1.3.4.2 gives the N source exceptions, each first edge matrix 2P_{U_a} of rank one.
Sum of absolute dimension changes Wm-2N+2L by telescoping, L=Ich, and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
L_b/N=100/539<1/2, so the deficit N-2L_b>0 and s_b<W_b m. The complex ratio 101/539 is not given, but the bit case carries the step.

S1.5.3 states M_out(rho(w))-M_in(w)=I_m and concludes H<-H+D on every row, scratch rows included, through the frame identity. The plan does not verify the identity (P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I), but it carries the step's content and role.
A=E_1 Pi E_2 gives exactly a interchanges plus O(V). Each edge shear is done by recursive interchanges, so a node makes exactly s recursive calls.
Children have volume V/W, so F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1). With s/W<m^tau, tau=1-2^{-50} from deficit >20*2^{-50} and log m<20, the geometric sum gives F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan reconstructs eight of the nine steps of the central saving: frames, labels, rank equals dimension change, the budget, the strict saving L_b/N=100/539, the endpoint identity, edges as recursive calls, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}. The weak link is C1. The bank-exchanging, scratch-restoring network is described, but its parameters (h=100, triples, N, m) are never given.
